items.evidence: After page.reload() the note is read back with expect(noteInput).toHaveValue(note) (diff line 96). That would fail if the customerUpdate mutation never ran.
Actor criterion: test.use({ actor: "customer" }) at line 16. Field shows the note after saving: line 88. Note survives a reload: lines 94-96.
No existing page object covers the customers list or customer details screens, and CUSTOMER and ORDERS_SCENARIO are imported from scenarios/orders.ts rather than copied.
No waitForTimeout, no sleeps and no fixed-delay polling. The waits are on URL, title and web-first assertions.
Imports test and expect from ../../fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache or dumps.

Elements are found by data-test-id or role and name. The Glide canvas is found by its own data-testid, because Glide grid rows have no test id or role locator. The save button and the toast are unique on the page or scoped to the Notifications region.
No API calls or UI set-up of data: the orders scenario already provides Ada Lovelace, and the spec only performs the story's own action.
No hard-coded ids. The customer is identified by CUSTOMER.email, CUSTOMER.firstName and CUSTOMER.lastName from the scenario.
The spec uses the stored session of the single-permission "customer" actor (user.manager@example.com). There is no UI login and no credentials appear in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports "exit 0: no errors" and the spec is at e2e/tests/customers/customer-note.spec.ts.

e2e/tests/customers/customer-note.spec.ts lines 25-33 and 58-66: every locator, plus the multi-step hover-and-click row opening, is defined inline in the spec instead of on a new customer page object in e2e/pages/ (the spec's own plan in specs/customer-note.md asks for one).
No page-object members were added, so this does not apply.
// Arrange at line 22 and // Act & Assert at line 35, around the test.step blocks, which is the suite's pattern.
One test with a test.step for each stage: find, open, write and save, field shows the note, survives a reload.
The title at line 19 describes the behaviour and carries #e2e.
The JSDoc block at lines 12-15 says what the spec covers.
All assertions are web-first. boundingBox() is used only to compute where to hover, not for an assertion.
Customer values and the scenario name come from the exported constants. The note text is the test's own input, and no money is compared.
No cleanup hooks, no delete-if-exists steps and no timestamped or random names.
No per-test timeouts or retries, no networkidle, and no waitForLoadState. waitForURL waits on a URL change, as the suite does.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.

e2e/tests/customers/customer-note.spec.ts lines 7-8, 23, 36, 56, 76, 86 and 92: generated boilerplate ("// spec: ...", "// seed: ...") and numbered step comments ("// 2. Find the customer from the customers list") that repeat the next test.step title instead of explaining why.

structured_output.summary: Submission fad76700 has no blockers and fails two minors (M1, M13). The spec runs as the single-permission customer actor on the orders scenario, saves a note on Ada Lovelace, and proves the note was saved by reading it back after a page reload. It type-checks cleanly. M1: all locators and the canvas hover-and-click needed to open a row are written inline instead of on a new customer page object. M13: the comments are generated step narration and boilerplate rather than explanations.
